name: get_routine_details
description: Fetch one or more routines' FULL if/then/else automation logic, as NuCore's compiled routine schema (the form create_or_update_routine's DSL compiles to): `status`/`control`/`schedule`/`cmd`/`var`/etc. nodes with real device/routine/variable ids, uom values, and GE/GT/IS/ISNOT/LE/LT-style op tokens. Explain it to the customer in plain language; to edit it, rewrite the logic as DSL per create_or_update_routine's grammar -- this compiled form is not valid `code`. Returns a list, one entry per requested id, in the same order as `ids` -- pass every routine id you need in one call rather than calling this once per routine (e.g. when confirming several candidate routines against a log entry, request all of their ids together). Any value whose uom is an index/enum type (25/146/148) is annotated with a real `label` string alongside the raw `value` (resolved from the actual device/command/property, not guessed) -- always prefer and relay `label` over the raw number when explaining a routine to the customer; if a value has no `label`, it's a plain number, not an unresolved enum. A `var` node also gets a real `name` resolved onto it. CRITICAL: a `var` node in `if` is always a COMPARISON (op is one of GT/GE/LT/LE/IS/ISNOT) -- describe it as a check. A `var` node in `then`/`else` is always an ASSIGNMENT (op is one of EQ/ADD=/SUB=/MUL=/DIV=/REM=/AND=/OR=/XOR=/RDM=/INIT), never a check, even though EQ reads like the English word "equals" -- it gets an `op_label` (e.g. "set equal to", "increase by") annotated onto it; always describe it using that label (e.g. "sets Watering_the_plants to 1"), never as "checks if ... equals". ROUTINES DATABASE only lists a routine's name/comment/referenced devices/referenced variables, never its actual logic -- call this tool for any 'what does this routine do', 'show me the full logic', or 'explain this routine' question, and before editing an existing routine's logic with create_or_update_routine. Each result also carries a best-effort `running_state` dict (omitted if the hub's runtime summary was unavailable for that routine) with its current `folder`/`status`/`lastRunTime`/`lastFinishTime`/`enabled`/`runAtStartup`/`running`/`nextScheduledRunTime` -- fresh as of this call, safe to answer 'is X enabled', 'is X running right now', or 'when did X last run' from directly, no separate tool call needed for those.

ids.description: The routines' real ids, exactly as shown in ROUTINES DATABASE -- never guessed. Put every routine you need detail for this turn into this one list -- never split them across separate calls.
